                            1Purpose

                            This document describes how to prepare a Windows computer for the Genomic Report Generation application, how to install and start it, which input files are required, and how to run a complete OncoPanel™ genomics study from the OncoPredictor outputs to the final Word report and deliverables package. It also explains the output folder structure, where the logs are written and how to resolve common problems.

                            2Scope

                            This guide applies to Genomic Report Generation version 1.0.0 running on Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit). It covers:

                            • Prerequisites and the installation of Python and R
                            • Installation of the application (Portable and Auto-install packages)
                            • The seven-step workflow, from OncoPredictor Output Collection to Final Report Packaging
                            • Inputs, outputs, logs, settings, troubleshooting and information for IT support

                            It does not cover the scientific interpretation of the results or the content of the R clustering script, the Excel template or the Word report template; these remain under their own procedures.

                            3Definitions and abbreviations

                            TermMeaning

                            Mutation reportMutation Excel report exported from OncoPredictor (sheet OncoPanel Results)

                            GenerateClusteringFile.RHelper R script that the clustering script loads with source()
                            g:Profiler / g:GOStPublic functional-enrichment web service used for the pathway analysis

                            Deliverables packageZip file with all outputs and a SHA-256 checksum manifest

                            SOCStandard of care (reference compounds in the clustering output)

                            4Responsibilities

                            RoleResponsibility
                            End user (scientist / report author)Prepares the inputs, runs the workflow, checks and finalises the report
                            Application ownerMaintains the application package, the default templates and this document
                            IT supportApproves the installation on company computers and allows the network addresses listed in section 6.4

                            5Overview of the application

                            Genomic Report Generation automates the OncoPanel™ genomics reporting workflow. It runs locally on the user's computer and opens in a Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge window. Nothing is published on the network: the application only listens on this computer (127.0.0.1). Each study is processed in seven steps:

                            StepName in the applicationWhat happensInput from the user
                            1OncoPredictor Output CollectionValidates the DiffEx and Mutation reports and stores them in the projectTwo Excel reports
                            2Clustering Script ExecutionRuns the clustering R script with the project paths filled inR script (helper and .tab optional)
                            3DiffEx Table GenerationCopies DiffEx columns A:P into Table 3 for DiffEx and writes the formulasExcel template
                            4Sensitivity Gene ExtractionExtracts the top 60 sensitivity and top 60 resistance genesNone
                            5g:Profiler Pathway AnalysisRuns g:GOSt for both gene lists and saves the result filesNone (internet needed)
                            6Word Report GenerationFills Table 3, the gene summaries and the report placeholdersWord template, report details
                            7Final Report PackagingPackages every deliverable into one zip with a checksum manifestNone

                            Every completed step is remembered. If a step fails, correct the cause and click Retry; completed steps are never repeated. Steps 2 and 5 can be skipped when R or internet access is not available.

                            6Prerequisites

                            6.1Computer requirements

                            ItemRequirementRemarks
                            Operating systemWindows 10 (version 1803 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit
                            Memory4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommendedLarge DiffEx files contain about 19,000 rows
                            Free disk space1 GB, plus about 50 MB per studyPortable package: about 600 MB after extraction
                            BrowserGoogle Chrome or Microsoft EdgeEdge is part of Windows; Chrome is used when installed
                            Administrator rightsNot requiredEverything installs for the current user only
                            Microsoft Word and ExcelOptionalOnly needed to open and review the outputs

                            6.2Software requirements

                            SoftwareVersionUsed forPortable packageAuto-install package
                            Python3.10 or newer (3.12.10 validated)Running the applicationIncludedInstalled automatically
                            R4.x (4.6.2 validated)Step 2 onlyIncludedInstalled automatically
                            R package dplyrCurrentClustering R scriptIncludedInstalled automatically
                            Python librariesSee backend\requirements.txtRunning the applicationIncludedInstalled automatically
                            Note: With either package the user does not need to install anything by hand. Section 8 describes the manual installation of Python and R for the cases where IT prefers to install them, or the computer has no internet access during setup.

                            6.3Packages delivered

                            PackageSizeRecommended whenWhat it needs
                            GenomicReport_Portable.zipabout 195 MBUsers must not install software, or the computer is offlineNothing; Python and R are inside the folder
                            GenomicReport_AutoInstall.zipabout 1 MBA small download is preferred and the computer has internetInternet on the first start; Python and R are installed for the current user

                            6.4Network access

                            The application needs internet access only for the following activities. The addresses are given in the steps where they are used:

                            • First start of the Auto-install package: downloads Python from python.org, R from cloud.r-project.org and the Python libraries from pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org.
                            • First run of Step 2: downloads missing R packages (dplyr) from cloud.r-project.org, unless already installed.
                            • Step 5: uses the g:Profiler service at biit.cs.ut.ee. On its first run the browser driver is downloaded from googlechromelabs.github.io and storage.googleapis.com.
                            • Launch OncoPredictor (optional, Step 1): opens the internal OncoPredictor portal.

                            7Installing the application

                            7.1Option A – Portable package (recommended)

                            The Portable package contains the application together with its own Python and R. Nothing is installed on the computer and nothing is downloaded.

                            1. Copy GenomicReport_Portable.zip to the computer, for example into Documents.
                            2. Right-click the zip file and choose Extract All…. Choose a short destination folder such as C:\Users\<user>\GenomicReport and click Extract. Do not start the application from inside the zip file.
                            3. Open the extracted folder GenomicReport_Portable. It contains:
                            GenomicReport_Portable\
├── Start-GenomicReport.bat      ← double-click to start
├── HOW-TO-RUN.txt
├── backend\                     application
├── docs\                        this guide (Word, PDF and HTML)
├── R\GenerateClusteringFile.R   built-in dummy helper
├── samples\                     sample assay (.tab) file
└── runtime\                     bundled Python 3.12 and R 4.6.2 (with dplyr)
                            1. Double-click Start-GenomicReport.bat. After a few seconds the application window opens with the welcome screen (section 9).

                            7.2Option B – Auto-install package

                            The Auto-install package is small. On the first start it installs whatever is missing, for the current user only and without administrator rights. The installers are downloaded from the official sites and their digital signatures are verified before they run.

                            1. Copy GenomicReport_AutoInstall.zip to the computer, right-click it, choose Extract All… and extract it to a short folder such as C:\Users\<user>\GenomicReport.
                            2. Open the extracted folder and double-click Start-GenomicReport.bat.
                            3. A setup window opens. Keep it open. The first start takes about 4 to 10 minutes depending on the internet speed:
                            • [1/4] If Python 3.10 or newer is not found, Python 3.12.10 is downloaded from https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.12.10/python-3.12.10-amd64.exe and installed silently to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Python312.
                            • [2/4] If R is not found, R 4.6.2 is downloaded from https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/R-4.6.2-win.exe (or, after a newer R release, from https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/old/4.6.2/R-4.6.2-win.exe) and installed silently to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\R\R-4.6.2. The R package dplyr is then installed from https://cloud.r-project.org.
                            • [3/4] A private Python environment is created in %LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration\venv.
                            • [4/4] The Python libraries are installed from https://pypi.org.
                            1. When Setup complete – starting the application… is displayed, the setup window closes and the application window opens.
                            2. Later starts skip the setup and open the application within a few seconds.
                            Important: If the setup reports that a download failed, the computer has no internet access or a company proxy blocks the addresses above. Connect to the internet, or ask IT to allow the addresses, and double-click Start-GenomicReport.bat again; the setup continues where it stopped. If R cannot be installed, the application still starts and Step 2 can be skipped.

                            8Installing Python and R manually (optional)

                            Skip this section when using the Portable or the Auto-install package. Follow it only when Python and R must be installed by hand, for example by IT. No administrator rights are needed when the options below are followed.

                            8.1Install Python

                            1. Open the Python 3.12.10 download page in a browser: https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31210/
                            2. Scroll down to Files and click Windows installer (64-bit). Do not use the Python install manager button at the top of the page. The direct download link is https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.12.10/python-3.12.10-amd64.exe
                            1. Double-click the downloaded file python-3.12.10-amd64.exe.
                            2. On the first screen of the installer, untick “Use admin privileges when installing py.exe”. Leaving this option ticked is what triggers the administrator prompt.
                            3. Tick “Add python.exe to PATH”.
                            4. Click Install Now. Python is installed to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312.
                            5. When Setup was successful is shown, click Close.
                            6. Check the installation: press Windows + R, type cmd and press Enter. In the Command Prompt type python --version and press Enter. The result must be Python 3.10 or higher.

                            8.2Install R

                            1. Open the CRAN download page for Windows in a browser: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/
                            2. Click Download R-4.6.2 for Windows. The direct download link is https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/R-4.6.2-win.exe. After a newer R version is released, version 4.6.2 is moved to https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/old/4.6.2/R-4.6.2-win.exe
                            1. Double-click the downloaded file R-4.6.2-win.exe.
                            2. If the installer asks for the installation mode, choose Install for me only (no administrator rights needed).
                            3. Select the language and click OK, then keep every default option and click Next on each page until Finish.
                            4. R is installed to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\R\R-4.6.2 (per user) or C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.2 (all users). Both are detected automatically.
                            5. Check the installation in a Command Prompt: "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\R\R-4.6.2\bin\Rscript.exe" --version
                            Note: R does not have to be added to PATH and the dplyr package does not have to be installed by hand. The application finds R through the Windows registry and installs missing R packages automatically the first time Step 2 runs.

                            8.3Then install the application

                            With Python and R installed, extract the Auto-install package and double-click Start-GenomicReport.bat (section 7.2). The setup detects the installed Python and R and only creates the Python environment.

                            9Starting and stopping the application

                            1. Double-click Start-GenomicReport.bat in the application folder.
                            2. The application opens in its own Chrome or Edge window at http://127.0.0.1:8765. If it is already running, the existing window is brought to the front instead of starting a second copy.
                            3. The welcome screen is shown on every start; no study is opened automatically.
                            ElementPurpose
                            Start a new projectCreates a new study (section 11.1)
                            Open a previous projectOpens the Projects page to continue an earlier study
                            How it worksOpens the built-in User Guide page
                            Left menuDashboard, Projects, Activity Log, User Guide and Settings
                            All systems readyGreen when R, the browser and the default project folder are found
                            Light theme / Dark themeSwitches the colour scheme

                            To stop the application, close its window. The background process stops by itself about five minutes later. If a Session expired message appears, close the window and start the application again.

                            10Inputs required

                            Prepare the following files before starting a study. They can be on a local drive, a mapped drive (for example K:) or a network share. The R script and the templates selected last are remembered and pre-filled for the next study.

                            InputFormatRequiredUsed inDescription
                            Project locationFolderYesNew projectWhere the study folder is created, for example D:\ or K:\Projects
                            DiffEx report.xlsx / .xlsmYesStep 1OncoPredictor output, for example …_Vemurafenib_13FEB23-Diffex-PROD.xlsx
                            Mutation report.xlsx / .xlsmYesStep 1OncoPredictor output with sheet OncoPanel Results; the analysis parameter (for example IC50) is read from cell D1
                            Clustering R script.rYes*Step 2For example EurofinsDiscovery_OncoPanel_Genomics_Client_Study_Clustering_Script_25Jan2023.r
                            GenerateClusteringFile.R.rOptionalStep 2The helper normally stored in K:\LabOperations\Oncopanel\QC support files. Empty: built-in dummy helper
                            Assay data file.tab / .txt / .tsv / .csvOptionalStep 2Tab-delimited assay data. Empty: a dummy file is generated from the Mutation report
                            Excel template.xlsx / .xlsmYesStep 3…_Client_Study_Mutations_and_Hotspots_Tables_Template_25Jan2023.xlsx (sheet Table 3 for DiffEx)
                            Word template.docxYesStep 6…_Client_Study_Report_Template_25Jan2023.docx
                            Report detailsTextOptionalStep 6Compound, analysis parameter, client name and order ID

                            * Step 2 can be skipped when R is not available. Every file is checked before it is used: full path, correct extension, not empty, at most 1 GB, and the expected sheets and header rows.

                            11Running a study end to end

                            The screenshots in this section show a complete example study for the compound Vemurafenib, created in P:\Vemurafenib_Study.

                            11.1Create a project

                            1. On the welcome screen click Start a new project, or click New project at the top right.
                            2. In Project location, type a folder or click the folder icon to browse. The right-hand panel shows the study folder and the sub-folders that will be created.
                            • Empty folder: used as the study folder.
                            • Drive or folder that already contains files: a new folder GenomicReport_<date>_<time> is created inside it.
                            • Existing study folder: the study is reopened and resumed.
                            1. Click Create project. The Dashboard opens for the new study.

                            The Dashboard shows the study name and folder, the overall progress, the current step, the execution time and the number of output files, errors and warnings. Below it are the Workflow with the seven steps, the Live activity panel and the Deliverables list.

                            11.2Step 1 – OncoPredictor Output Collection

                            1. Optional: click Launch OncoPredictor to open the OncoPredictor portal (https://automationtools-panlabsus.eurofinsdiscovery.net/) and download the DiffEx and Mutation reports of the study.
                            2. In DiffEx report (.xlsx) from OncoPredictor, type the path or click the folder icon and select the DiffEx report.
                            3. In Mutation report (.xlsx) from OncoPredictor, select the Mutation report.
                            1. Click Import files. Both files are validated (swapped or wrong files are detected) and moved into <study>\OncoPredictor.
                            Note: By default the selected reports are moved into the study folder. To copy them instead, switch off Move the selected OncoPredictor files into the project in Settings (section 15).

                            11.3Step 2 – Clustering Script Execution

                            1. In 1 · Clustering R script (.r), select the clustering R script.
                            2. Optional: in 2 · GenerateClusteringFile.R, select the helper script. Leave it empty to use the built-in dummy helper.
                            3. Optional: in 3 · Assay data file (.tab), select the assay data file. Leave it empty to generate a dummy file from the Mutation report.
                            4. Check the R line under the fields: it shows the Rscript.exe that will be used.
                            1. Click Run R script. The step shows the elapsed time while R runs (maximum 60 minutes, configurable).
                            2. When R has finished, the number of output files is shown.

                            The original R script is never changed. A copy is written to <study>\Clustering in which the fixed paths are replaced:

                            Line in the original scriptLine in the copy that is run
                            working_directory <- "C:/Users/Folder/"working_directory <- "<study>/Clustering/"
                            client_data_fn <- paste0(working_directory, "file.tab")client_data_fn <- paste0(working_directory, "<assay file>")
                            source("K:/LabOperations/Oncopanel/QC support files/GenerateClusteringFile.R")source("<selected helper or built-in dummy>")
                            (added at the top)Installs missing R packages such as dplyr
                            Important: The built-in GenerateClusteringFile.R and the generated .tab file are placeholders until the real files are available. Their outputs are marked DUMMY and must not be used in a client report. When the real files are available, select them in Step 2 and click Re-run from here.

                            11.4Step 3 – DiffEx Table Generation

                            1. Check that Mutations & Hotspots Excel template shows the correct template. It is pre-filled from Settings; click the folder icon to choose another one.
                            2. Click Run step.

                            DiffEx columns A:P are copied into the sheet Table 3 for DiffEx and the formulas are generated for every row. The workbook is saved in <study>\DiffEx. This takes about one minute for 19,000 rows.

                            11.5Step 4 – Sensitivity Gene Extraction

                            1. Click Run step. No input is needed.

                            The genes are ranked and the top 60 sensitivity genes (column AE) and top 60 resistance genes (column AF) are written to Top60_Sensitivity_Genes.txt and Top60_Resistance_Genes.txt in <study>\DiffEx.

                            11.6Step 5 – g:Profiler Pathway Analysis

                            1. Make sure the computer is connected to the internet. The step uses g:GOSt at https://biit.cs.ut.ee/gprofiler/gost
                            2. Click Run step. A browser window may open briefly while the queries run; do not close it.

                            Both gene lists are submitted in parallel with organism Homo sapiens and ordered query. When there are no significant results, the query is repeated with All results. If the browser automation fails, the official g:Profiler API is used instead. The result CSV files and a snapshot image are saved in <study>\GProfiler\Sensitivity and <study>\GProfiler\Resistance.

                            Tip: Without internet access, click Skip and run Step 5 later with Retry.

                            11.7Step 6 – Word Report Generation

                            1. Check that Word report template (.docx) shows the correct template.
                            2. Optional: fill in the report details. Fields left empty are handled as described below.
                            3. Click Run step.
                            FieldPlaceholder in the templateIf left empty
                            CompoundCLIENTTESTAGENTTaken from the DiffEx file name (for example Vemurafenib)
                            Analysis parameterANALYSISPARAMETERRead from cell D1 of the Mutation report (for example IC50)
                            ClientCLIENTNAMEPlaceholder stays in the report for manual completion
                            Order IDSTUDYNUMBERPlaceholder stays in the report for manual completion
                            Date (automatic)MONTH DAY, YEARAlways today's date

                            11.8Step 7 – Final Report Packaging

                            1. Click Run step.

                            All deliverables are collected into <study>_Deliverables_<date>_<time>.zip in <study>\Reports, together with a manifest.json that lists the SHA-256 checksum of every file.

                            11.9Running all remaining steps at once

                            Instead of clicking Run step on every step, click Start workflow (or Resume workflow) at the top of the Dashboard. The remaining steps run in order and pause only when an input is missing.

                            ButtonEffect
                            Start workflow / Resume workflowRuns all remaining steps in order
                            Run step / Import files / Run R scriptRuns only this step
                            RetryRuns a failed step again after the cause has been corrected
                            SkipSkips an optional step (Step 2 or Step 5)
                            Re-run from hereResets this step and all following steps and runs them again
                            StopStops the running step, including the R process
                            Open project folderOpens the study folder in Windows Explorer

                            11.10Collecting the results

                            1. In the Deliverables panel on the right of the Dashboard, click the open icon next to a file to open it, or the folder icon to show it in Windows Explorer.
                            2. Review the Word report, complete any remaining manual sections and send the deliverables package as required.

                            12Expected outputs

                            12.1Study folder structure

                            Each study folder contains six sub-folders. The example below is the complete study P:\Vemurafenib_Study:

├── Clustering\
│   ├── EurofinsDiscovery_..._Clustering_Script_25Jan2023_Vemurafenib_Study.r
│   ├── Vemurafenib_assay_data_DUMMY.tab
│   ├── Vemurafenib_assay_data_DUMMY_Clustering_Data.csv
│   ├── Vemurafenib_assay_data_DUMMY_Clustering_Dendrogram.png

├── DiffEx\
│   ├── EurofinsDiscovery_OncoPanel_Genomics_Vemurafenib_Study_
│   │       Mutations_and_Hotspots_Tables_05Nov2026.xlsx

│   ├── Top60_Resistance_Genes.txt

├── GProfiler\
│   ├── Sensitivity\  Vemurafenib_Study_gProfiler_Sensitivity.csv / .png

                            12.2Description of the output files

                            FolderFileStepDescription
                            OncoPredictorDiffEx and Mutation reports1The imported input reports
                            Clustering<script>_<study>.r2The copy of the R script that was run, with the study paths
                            Clustering<compound>_assay_data….tab2The assay data used (selected file or generated DUMMY file)
                            Clustering*_Clustering_Data.csv, *_Ranked_SOC_Compounds.csv, *_Dendrogram.png2Outputs of GenerateClusteringFile (the real helper may use other names)
                            DiffEx…_Mutations_and_Hotspots_Tables_<date>.xlsx3Filled Excel template with Table 3 for DiffEx
                            DiffExTop60_Sensitivity_Genes.txt, Top60_Resistance_Genes.txt4The two gene lists sent to g:Profiler
                            DiffExranked_genes.json4Gene ranking used by Steps 5 and 6
                            GProfiler<study>_gProfiler_Sensitivity.csv / .png, …_Resistance.csv / .png5g:GOSt results and snapshots
                            Reports…_Report_<date>.docx6The completed Word report
                            Reports<study>_Deliverables_<date>_<time>.zip7All deliverables with manifest.json (SHA-256)
                            Logsactivity_log.txt, clustering_R_console.logAllLogs of the study (section 13)
                            • Output names follow the template names: _Template is removed, Client_Study is replaced by the study name and the template date is replaced by today's date (for example 05Nov2026).
                            • If a full path would be longer than Windows allows, a shorter name such as <study>_Report_05Nov2026.docx is used.
                            • Running a step again overwrites the outputs of that step; input files are never modified.

                            12.3Examples of the outputs

                            13Logs and audit trail

                            13.1Where to find the logs

                            LogLocationContent
                            Live activityDashboard, right-hand panelProgress of the open study, newest first
                            Activity Log pageLeft menu → Activity LogAudit trail of all studies; searchable and filtered by level
                            Study activity log<study>\Logs\activity_log.txtEvery action of the study with time, level and details
                            R console log<study>\Logs\clustering_R_console.logEverything R printed in Step 2, including R errors
                            Server log%LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration\server.logStart-up messages and unexpected errors
                            Audit database%LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration\audit.dbStudies, step status, files and audit trail
                            Settings%LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration\settings.jsonSaved settings and remembered paths

                            To open the application-data folder, press Windows + R, type %LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration and press Enter.

                            13.2Live activity panel

                            While a study runs, every action appears in the Live activity panel on the Dashboard.

                            13.3Activity Log page

                            1. Click Activity Log in the left menu.
                            2. Type in the search box to find an action, a file, a study or a user.
                            3. Click Success, Info, Warning or Error to show only that level.

                            13.4Reading activity_log.txt

                            Each line contains the date and time, the level (INFO, SUCCESS, WARNING or ERROR), the action and the details. Extract from the example study:

                            2026-11-05 17:54:06  [SUCCESS]  Project created  |  P:\Vemurafenib_Study
2026-11-05 17:55:40  [SUCCESS]  DiffEx file found  |  …Diffex-PROD.xlsx (18,824 probes)
2026-11-05 17:55:44  [SUCCESS]  Mutation report found  |  …Mutation-PROD.xlsx (242 cell lines)
2026-11-05 17:56:15  [WARNING]  Using the built-in DUMMY GenerateClusteringFile.R

                            14Managing studies

                            1. Click Projects in the left menu. Every study processed on this computer is listed with its status (Complete, In progress or Attention), its folder and its progress.
                            2. Click a study card to open it on the Dashboard, then click Resume workflow to continue where it stopped.
                            3. To remove a study from the list, click the bin icon. The study folder on disk is not deleted.
                            Tip: A study can also be opened with the Open a previous project… list at the top of the Dashboard, or by choosing its folder in the Create project dialog.

                            15Settings

                            Click Settings in the left menu, change the values and click Save. The System health panel on the same page shows whether R, the browser and the default project location were found.

                            16Troubleshooting

                            Message or symptomCauseAction
                            “Python 3.10 or newer was not found”Python missing and could not be installedInstall Python (section 8.1) and start again
                            “Download failed” or “Installing the libraries failed”No internet, or a proxy blocks the download sitesConnect to the internet or ask IT to allow the addresses in section 6.4
                            Administrator credentials requested, or the start is blockedCompany security policyUse the Portable package, or ask IT to approve the application (section 17)
                            “R is not installed on this computer”Rscript.exe not foundInstall R (section 8.2) or click Skip on Step 2
                            “Could not find the input path lines in the R script”The script has no working_directory / client_data_fn linesRestore those two lines in the script
                            “Could not find a source("…GenerateClusteringFile.R") line”The helper file name differs from the name in the scriptSelect a helper with the same file name
                            “R script failed (exit code …)”Error inside the R codeRead Logs\clustering_R_console.log, correct it, click Retry
                            “… does not look like a Mutation report”DiffEx and Mutation reports swapped, or wrong fileSelect the correct files
                            “Output path is too long for Windows”Very long study folder pathChoose a shorter project location
                            Step 5 failsNo internet, or g:Profiler unavailableCheck the connection and click Retry, or Skip
                            “Session expired”The application restarted while the window was openClose the window and start the application again
                            The window does not openStart-up errorRead server.log (section 13.1)

                            17Security and information for IT

                            TopicDetail
                            Administrator rightsNot required. All components install and run for the current user
                            Network listener127.0.0.1:8765 only; not reachable from other computers
                            Access controlRandom session token per start, Host and Origin checks, strict Content-Security-Policy
                            File accessReads the files the user selects; writes only into the study folders and the application-data folder
                            Input checksFile type and size limits, sheet and header validation, protection against formula injection
                            InstallersOfficial python.org and CRAN installers; the Authenticode signature is verified before they run
                            Writes to%LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python and …\R (Auto-install), %TEMP%, and the study folders
                            StartsChrome or Edge (application window and Step 5), Rscript.exe (Step 2)
                            AuditEvery action is recorded with the Windows user name in audit.db and Logs\activity_log.txt
                            Allow-listingBy folder, or by file hash (Get-FileHash <file> gives the SHA-256)

                            Silent installation commands, for IT deployment of Python and R for the current user:

                            python-3.12.10-amd64.exe /quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1 Include_launcher=0 Shortcuts=0
R-4.6.2-win.exe /VERYSILENT /CURRENTUSER /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /NOICONS
                            Important: Step 2 runs the R script selected by the user. Select R scripts only from a controlled, trusted location.

                            18Updating and uninstalling

                            TaskHow
                            Update the applicationClose the application and replace the application folder with the new version. Studies, settings and logs are kept
                            Uninstall the applicationDelete the application folder
                            Remove settings, logs and the Python environmentDelete %LOCALAPPDATA%\GenomicReportGeneration
                            Remove Python and R (Auto-install)Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Python 3.12.10 (64-bit) and R for Windows 4.6.2 → Uninstall
                            StudiesStudy folders are never deleted automatically
